evals.prompt: I need to refactor a Vue 3 component that has comparisons, collection length checks, and function calls in template directives, bindings, and interpolation. Keep the public props the same, and do not invent a reusable abstraction unless the component actually repeats the pattern.
evals.expected_output: The agent scans the full template, moves component-wide derived rendering values into named computed state or view-model fields, and uses named side-effect-free helpers for logic that needs template-local bindings while preserving the component API.
expectations: The workflow inspects nearby component conventions before choosing the final shape.
The workflow uses named computed state or view-model fields for component-wide values and permits named side-effect-free helper calls for template-local bindings.
The workflow preserves existing props, emits, slots, and Vue-specific styling hooks unless the task requires a change.
The workflow avoids adding generic abstractions for a small fixed UI.

evals.prompt: Build a small openable Vue component with TypeScript. It should support v-model for its open state and emit regular confirm and cancel actions. Keep the public component contract clear.
evals.expected_output: The agent should use defineModel only for the two-way open state, call out the defineModel default caveat, and use defineEmits for regular confirm and cancel actions.
expectations: The workflow uses defineModel only for the real v-model contract.
The workflow does not use defineModel for ordinary submit, cancel, click, or analytics events.
The workflow uses defineEmits for regular confirm and cancel actions.
The workflow keeps the component's props, emits, and model contract explicit.

evals.prompt: Review this Nuxt page change that mixes useFetch calls, a Pinia store mutation, and a child Vue component prop cleanup. I only want component-level feedback from the Vue skill.
evals.expected_output: The agent should keep the Vue skill scoped to the child component surface and route Nuxt data fetching, Pinia state, and tests to local conventions or more specific skills only when those skills are available.
expectations: The workflow limits Vue skill feedback to component props, emits, Vue template mechanics, Vue-specific styling bindings, and component TypeScript.
The workflow treats Nuxt useFetch or app-level data fetching as outside this skill's core scope.
The workflow treats Pinia state shape and store mutations as outside this skill's core scope.
The workflow recommends repository test conventions or a unit-testing skill if one is available, without assuming a specific skill is installed.

evals.prompt: This Vue component now has repeated open/close state, Escape key handling, and derived aria IDs. Extract a composable if that is justified, but do not hide component markup or styling rules inside it.
evals.expected_output: The agent should extract only reusable state/effect logic into a `use*` composable, return a plain object of refs/computed values/functions, keep markup and styling in the component, and own cleanup for listeners or effects.
expectations: The workflow extracts a composable only when there is a reusable named behavior or real component complexity.
The workflow names the composable with a `use` prefix.
The workflow keeps markup, slots, and styling decisions in the component instead of hiding them inside the composable.
The workflow returns a plain object containing refs, computed values, and functions so destructuring remains reactive.
The workflow owns cleanup for event listeners, observers, timers, or subscriptions created by the composable.

evals.prompt: Update a Vue component that uses <style module>. Its button binds separate $style classes for structure, active state, and disabled state. Keep the same visual states and the Vue styling system.
evals.expected_output: The agent should keep one structural $style class, use literal global state classes or attributes, and define their selectors under the module class with :global(...).
expectations: The workflow keeps one $style structural class on the button.
The workflow uses literal global state classes or attributes instead of module-local state classes.
The workflow nests global state selectors under the structural module class with :global(...).
The workflow preserves <style module> instead of switching the Vue component to another styling system.
The workflow does not use useCssModule only to pass presentation classes through render configuration.

evals.prompt: Refactor rendering in a Vue component. Its scoped slot exposes item.createdAt only inside #item, and a v-for uses both row and index to render a display label. There is no prepared display field for either case. The component also computes button disabled state inline from isSaving and items.length. Preserve behavior and the component structure.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses named side-effect-free helpers for the local slot/v-for values and a named computed value for component-wide disabled state.
expectations: The workflow keeps local slot and v-for arguments available to named side-effect-free helpers.
The workflow does not add components or state solely to eliminate those helper calls.
The workflow moves component-wide derived disabled state into a named computed value.
The workflow preserves event-handler conventions and existing component behavior.
